pergunta: Why can counting total area under formal protection overestimate actual conservation outcomes?
gabarito: Because area metrics ignore management effectiveness, enforcement, funding, and allowed use categories; many designated areas permit direct use or suffer poor resourcing, so nominal coverage may not reflect real biodiversity protection.
resposta_historica_amazoniaexpert: Counting total area under formal protection can overestimate actual conservation outcomes because it does not consider the effectiveness of management and the degree to which protected areas are actually conserved. The SPA reports highlight that evaluating the effectiveness of protected area management is a key element in progress towards achieving the Convention on Biological Diversity's (CBD) Strategic Plan and its Aichi Targets, especially Target 11, which addresses the contribution of a protected area system that is managed effectively and equitably. The reports also mention that PADDD has been occurring for years and has grown over time, impacting the achievement of the CBD land protection goal in some countries. This indicates that simply counting total area under formal protection does not accurately reflect actual conservation outcomes.
resposta_rag: Counting total area under formal protection can overestimate actual conservation outcomes because it does not consider the effectiveness of management, which is a key element in progress towards achieving the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) Strategic Plan and its Aichi Targets. The assessment of effective protection includes evaluating design aspects, adequacy and appropriateness of management systems and processes, as well as delivery of protected area objectives (Hockings et al., 2015). Additionally, the extent of coverage and categories of protection can be misleading because it does not consider changes in the protected areas' limits, size, or category over time. Studies have found that historically, the world has lost hundreds of thousands of square kilometers of protected land through PADDD (Protected Areas Downgrading, Downsizing, and Degazettement) processes, which can significantly impact conservation outcomes. Furthermore, there are significant challenges related to protected area resourcing and biodiversity protection effectiveness tracking, as well as a lack of resources in the Neotropics compared to other biogeographical realms (Coad et al., 2019).
